nodes.name: Similarity graph
nodes.statement: Given data $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with pairwise similarities $s_{ij} \geq 0$, the similarity graph $G=(V,E)$ has a vertex $v_i$ for each $x_i$ and an edge weighted by $s_{ij}$ when $s_{ij}$ is positive (or above a threshold).
nodes.statement_clean: Graph representation where each data point is a vertex and edges are weighted by pairwise similarity.

nodes.name: Weighted adjacency matrix
nodes.statement: For an undirected weighted graph $G$ with weights $w_{ij} = w_{ji} \geq 0$, the weighted adjacency matrix is $W = (w_{ij})_{i,j=1,\ldots,n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetric matrix of edge weights of the graph.

nodes.name: Degree and degree matrix
nodes.statement: The degree of vertex $v_i$ is $d_i = \sum_{j=1}^n w_{ij}$. The degree matrix $D$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $d_1,\ldots,d_n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Vertex degree is the sum of incident weights; the degree matrix is diagonal of degrees.

nodes.name: Indicator vector and volume of a subset
nodes.statement: For $A \subset V$, $\charfct_A \in \R^n$ has $f_i = 1$ if $v_i \in A$, $0$ otherwise. Two size measures: $|A|$ (number of vertices) and $\vol(A) = \sum_{i \in A} d_i$ (sum of incident edge weights).
nodes.statement_clean: Indicator vector marks set membership; cardinality and volume measure the size of a vertex subset.

nodes.name: Connected component and partition
nodes.statement: $A \subset V$ is connected if any two vertices in $A$ are joined by a path in $A$; it is a connected component if also no edge connects $A$ to $\bar A$. Sets $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ form a partition of $V$ if pairwise disjoint and $A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_k = V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Connected components and partitions of the vertex set.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-neighborhood graph
nodes.statement: Connect points whose pairwise distance is smaller than $\epsilon$. Usually treated as an unweighted graph since all connected distances are at most $\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph where points within distance epsilon are connected.

nodes.name: $k$-nearest neighbor graph
nodes.statement: Connect $v_i,v_j$ by an undirected edge if $v_j$ is among the $k$-nearest neighbors of $v_i$ OR if $v_i$ is among the $k$-nearest neighbors of $v_j$; weight by $s_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph where each point is connected to its k nearest neighbors (symmetrized by OR).

nodes.name: Mutual $k$-nearest neighbor graph
nodes.statement: Connect $v_i,v_j$ if BOTH $v_i$ is among the $k$-nearest neighbors of $v_j$ AND $v_j$ is among the $k$-nearest neighbors of $v_i$; weight by $s_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetrized k-NN graph using AND rather than OR.

nodes.name: Fully connected graph
nodes.statement: Connect all pairs with positive similarity, weighted by $s_{ij}$. Common choice: Gaussian similarity $s(x_i,x_j) = \exp(-\|x_i-x_j\|^2/(2\sigma^2))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Graph that connects all pairs, typically with Gaussian similarity.

nodes.name: Unnormalized graph Laplacian
nodes.statement: $\Lun = D - W$, where $D$ is the degree matrix and $W$ the weighted adjacency matrix.
nodes.statement_clean: L equals degree matrix minus adjacency matrix.

nodes.name: Normalized graph Laplacians $\Lsym$ and $\Lrw$
nodes.statement: $\Lsym := D^{-1/2} \Lun D^{-1/2} = I - D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2}$ (symmetric) and $\Lrw := D^{-1} \Lun = I - D^{-1} W$ (random-walk).
nodes.statement_clean: Two normalized variants of the graph Laplacian: symmetric and random-walk.

nodes.name: Cut
nodes.statement: $\Cut(A_1,\ldots,A_k) := \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k W(A_i, \bar A_i)$, where $W(A,B) = \sum_{i\in A, j\in B} w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Total weight of edges crossing a partition (with factor 1/2).

nodes.name: RatioCut
nodes.statement: $\Ratiocut(A_1,\ldots,A_k) := \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{W(A_i, \bar A_i)}{|A_i|} = \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{\Cut(A_i,\bar A_i)}{|A_i|}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cut value normalized by cluster cardinalities to balance cluster sizes.

nodes.name: Normalized cut $\Ncut$
nodes.statement: $\Ncut(A_1,\ldots,A_k) := \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{W(A_i, \bar A_i)}{\vol(A_i)} = \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{\Cut(A_i,\bar A_i)}{\vol(A_i)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cut value normalized by cluster volumes to balance edge mass.

nodes.name: MinMaxCut
nodes.statement: $\MinmaxCut(A_1,\ldots,A_k) := \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{\Cut(A_i,\bar A_i)}{W(A_i,A_i)}$, normalizing the cut by within-cluster similarity.
nodes.statement_clean: Cut criterion with denominator equal to within-cluster similarity.

nodes.name: Random walk transition matrix and stationary distribution
nodes.statement: $P = D^{-1} W$ has entries $p_{ij} = w_{ij}/d_i$. If the graph is connected and non-bipartite, the unique stationary distribution is $\pi_i = d_i / \vol(V)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Markov-chain transition matrix on the graph and its stationary distribution.

nodes.name: Commute distance
nodes.statement: The commute distance $c_{ij}$ between $v_i$ and $v_j$ is the expected time the random walk takes to travel from $v_i$ to $v_j$ and back. Also called resistance distance.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected round-trip time of the random walk between two vertices.

nodes.name: Generalized inverse $\Lun^\dagger$
nodes.statement: Writing $L = U \Lambda U'$, define $L^\dagger := U \Lambda^\dagger U'$ where $\Lambda^\dagger$ has entries $1/\lambda_i$ when $\lambda_i \neq 0$ and $0$ otherwise. Entries: $l_{ij}^\dagger = \sum_{k=2}^n \frac{1}{\lambda_k} u_{ik} u_{jk}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse of the unnormalized Laplacian.

nodes.name: Canonical (principal) angles
nodes.statement: For $p$-dimensional subspaces $\Vcal_1,\Vcal_2 \subset \R^d$ with orthonormal column matrices $V_1,V_2$, the cosines $\cos\Theta_i$ of the principal angles are the singular values of $V_1' V_2$. $\sin\mathbf{\Theta}(\Vcal_1,\Vcal_2)$ is the diagonal matrix of sines of these angles.
nodes.statement_clean: Principal angles between two subspaces, defined via singular values of a Gramian.

nodes.name: Properties of $\Lun$
nodes.statement: (1) For all $f \in \R^n$, $f' \Lun f = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(f_i-f_j)^2$. (2) $\Lun$ is symmetric and PSD. (3) Smallest eigenvalue is $0$ with eigenvector $\charfct$. (4) $\Lun$ has $n$ non-negative real eigenvalues $0 = \lambda_1 \leq \cdots \leq \lambda_n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quadratic form, symmetry, positive semi-definiteness, and non-negative eigenvalues of L.

nodes.name: Number of connected components and the spectrum of $\Lun$
nodes.statement: For undirected graph with non-negative weights, the multiplicity of eigenvalue $0$ of $\Lun$ equals the number $k$ of connected components $A_1,\ldots,A_k$, and the eigenspace of $0$ is spanned by the indicator vectors $\charfct_{A_1},\ldots,\charfct_{A_k}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 equals the number of connected components; eigenvectors are component indicators.

nodes.name: Properties of $\Lsym$ and $\Lrw$
nodes.statement: (1) $f' \Lsym f = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(f_i/\sqrt{d_i} - f_j/\sqrt{d_j})^2$. (2) $(\lambda,u)$ eig-pair of $\Lrw$ iff $(\lambda, D^{1/2}u)$ is for $\Lsym$. (3) $(\lambda,u)$ eig-pair of $\Lrw$ iff $\Lun u = \lambda D u$. (4) $0$ is eigenvalue with $\charfct$ for $\Lrw$ and $D^{1/2}\charfct$ for $\Lsym$. (5) Both PSD with $n$ non-negative eigenvalues.
nodes.statement_clean: Quadratic-form, eigenvalue-correspondence and PSD properties of the normalized Laplacians.

nodes.name: Number of connected components and spectra of $\Lsym, \Lrw$
nodes.statement: Multiplicity of eigenvalue $0$ of both $\Lrw$ and $\Lsym$ equals the number $k$ of connected components. For $\Lrw$ the $0$-eigenspace is spanned by $\charfct_{A_i}$; for $\Lsym$ by $D^{1/2}\charfct_{A_i}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Connected-components characterization for normalized Laplacians.

nodes.name: $\Ncut$ via transition probabilities
nodes.statement: For $G$ connected and non-bipartite, with $X_0$ in stationary distribution $\pi$: $\Ncut(A,\bar A) = P(\bar A | A) + P(A | \bar A)$ where $P(B|A) := P(X_1 \in B | X_0 \in A)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Ncut equals the sum of conditional transition probabilities between A and its complement.

nodes.name: Commute distance via $\Lun^\dagger$
nodes.statement: For connected undirected $G$: $c_{ij} = \vol(V)(l_{ii}^\dagger - 2 l_{ij}^\dagger + l_{jj}^\dagger) = \vol(V)(e_i - e_j)' \Lun^\dagger (e_i - e_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Commute distance can be computed from the pseudo-inverse of the Laplacian.

nodes.name: Davis-Kahan theorem
nodes.statement: For symmetric $A,H \in \R^{n \times n}$ and $\tilde A := A + H$, with $S_1 \subset \R$, let $V_1, \tilde V_1$ be the spectral projections for $A, \tilde A$ on $S_1$ and $\delta = \min\{|\lambda - s| : \lambda \notin S_1$ eigenvalue of $A, s \in S_1\}$. Then $d(V_1,\tilde V_1) := \|\sin\mathbf{\Theta}(V_1,\tilde V_1)\| \leq \|H\|/\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: The angle between perturbed and unperturbed eigenspaces is bounded by the perturbation norm divided by the spectral gap.

nodes.name: Rayleigh-Ritz theorem
nodes.statement: The minimum of $f' L f$ over $f \perp \charfct$ with $\|f\|^2 = n$ is achieved at the eigenvector corresponding to the second smallest eigenvalue of $L$. More generally, $\min_{H'H=I} \Tr(H'LH)$ is attained when columns of $H$ are the first $k$ eigenvectors of $L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Trace and quadratic-form minimization over orthonormal constraints is solved by the smallest eigenvectors.

nodes.name: Mincut problem
nodes.statement: Given similarity graph with adjacency $W$ and integer $k$, find a partition $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ minimizing $\Cut(A_1,\ldots,A_k) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k W(A_i,\bar A_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find a k-partition of the graph that minimizes the total cut weight.

nodes.name: RatioCut minimization
nodes.statement: $\min_{A_1,\ldots,A_k} \Ratiocut(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$. Equivalent matrix form: $\min_{H} \Tr(H' \Lun H)$ s.t. $H'H = I$, $H$ as cardinality-normalized indicator matrix. NP-hard combinatorial problem.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the size-balanced cut criterion over all k-partitions; NP-hard.

nodes.name: Ncut minimization
nodes.statement: $\min_{A_1,\ldots,A_k} \Ncut(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$. Equivalent: $\min_H \Tr(H' \Lun H)$ s.t. $H'DH = I$, $H$ as volume-normalized indicator matrix. NP-hard.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the volume-balanced normalized cut over all k-partitions.

nodes.name: Relaxed RatioCut (trace minimization)
nodes.statement: $\min_{H \in \R^{n \times k}} \Tr(H' \Lun H)$ subject to $H' H = I$. The solution is given by $H$ whose columns are the first $k$ eigenvectors of $\Lun$ (Rayleigh-Ritz).
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral relaxation of RatioCut: continuous trace minimization solved by the bottom-k eigenvectors of L.

nodes.name: Relaxed Ncut (generalized eigenproblem)
nodes.statement: $\min_{T \in \R^{n \times k}} \Tr(T' \Lsym T)$ subject to $T'T = I$. Equivalently, find first $k$ eigenvectors of $\Lrw$ or generalized eigenvectors of $\Lun u = \lambda D u$.
nodes.statement_clean: Continuous relaxation of Ncut leads to a generalized eigenproblem solved by bottom-k eigenvectors of Lrw.

nodes.name: Unnormalized spectral clustering
nodes.statement: Compute the first $k$ eigenvectors of the unnormalized Laplacian $\Lun$, embed each vertex as a row of $U \in \R^{n\times k}$, then run $k$-means on the embedded points.
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral clustering using bottom-k eigenvectors of L followed by k-means.

nodes.name: Normalized spectral clustering (Shi-Malik)
nodes.statement: Solve the generalized eigenproblem $\Lun u = \lambda D u$ for the first $k$ eigenvectors, embed each vertex as a row of $U$, then run $k$-means.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalized spectral clustering using generalized eigenvectors of L (equivalent to eigenvectors of Lrw).

nodes.name: Normalized spectral clustering (Ng-Jordan-Weiss)
nodes.statement: Compute first $k$ eigenvectors of $\Lsym$, row-normalize the matrix to obtain $T$ with $t_{ij} = u_{ij}/(\sum_k u_{ik}^2)^{1/2}$, then $k$-means on rows of $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalized spectral clustering using row-normalized eigenvectors of the symmetric normalized Laplacian.

nodes.name: $k$-means algorithm
nodes.statement: Standard centroid-based clustering used as the post-processing step on the spectral embedding $(y_i)_{i=1}^n \in \R^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical k-means clustering used as final step in spectral pipelines.

nodes.name: Proof of Properties of $\Lun$
nodes.statement: Part (1) by direct expansion of $f'\Lun f = f'D f - f'W f$. Parts (2)-(4) follow from (1) and symmetry of $W,D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Direct algebraic expansion of the quadratic form, then derive remaining parts from it.

nodes.name: Proof of components vs $\Lun$ spectrum
nodes.statement: Case $k=1$: $f'\Lun f = 0$ forces $f$ constant on the connected component. For $k$ components, $\Lun$ is block-diagonal and the result follows.
nodes.statement_clean: Case analysis (k=1, then general k) using block-diagonal structure.

nodes.name: Proof of properties of $\Lsym$ and $\Lrw$
nodes.statement: Parts (1)-(5) proved by algebraic manipulations of the eigenvalue equations and reuse of Proposition \ref{prop-unnorm}.
nodes.statement_clean: Algebraic manipulation of the eigenvalue equations.

nodes.name: Proof of components vs normalized Laplacian spectrum
nodes.statement: Analogous to the proof for $\Lun$, using Proposition \ref{prop-norm} to translate eigenvalue/eigenvector relationships between $\Lun$, $\Lrw$, and $\Lsym$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduce to the unnormalized case via the eigenvalue correspondence.

nodes.name: Proof of $\Ncut$ via transition probabilities
nodes.statement: Compute joint $P(X_0 \in A, X_1 \in B)$ using $\pi_i p_{ij} = w_{ij}/\vol(V)$, then the conditional $P(X_1 \in B | X_0 \in A)$, and conclude with the definition of $\Ncut$.
nodes.statement_clean: Compute joint and conditional transition probabilities under stationarity.

nodes.name: Quadratic form of $\Lun$
nodes.statement: $f' \Lun f = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i,j=1}^n w_{ij} (f_i - f_j)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quadratic form of unnormalized Laplacian as weighted sum of squared differences.

nodes.name: RatioCut indicator vector for $k=2$
nodes.statement: $f_i = \sqrt{|\bar A|/|A|}$ if $v_i \in A$, $-\sqrt{|A|/|\bar A|}$ if $v_i \in \bar A$. Then $f \perp \charfct$ and $\|f\|^2 = n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Encoding of a binary partition that turns RatioCut into f' L f.

nodes.name: $f' \Lun f = |V| \cdot \Ratiocut(A,\bar A)$
nodes.statement: With $f$ defined as in EP1.2, the quadratic form satisfies $f' \Lun f = |V| \cdot \Ratiocut(A,\bar A)$, expressing RatioCut as a Laplacian quadratic form.
nodes.statement_clean: Reformulation of RatioCut as f' L f for the indicator-style vector.

nodes.name: Ncut indicator vector for $k=2$
nodes.statement: $f_i = \sqrt{\vol(\bar A)/\vol(A)}$ if $v_i \in A$, $-\sqrt{\vol(A)/\vol(\bar A)}$ if $v_i \in \bar A$. Then $(Df)' \charfct = 0$, $f' D f = \vol(V)$, $f' \Lun f = \vol(V) \cdot \Ncut(A,\bar A)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Volume-weighted indicator for binary Ncut, leading to the generalized eigenproblem.

nodes.name: Toy example: mixture of four Gaussians on $\R$
nodes.statement: 200 points sampled from a 1D mixture of four Gaussians, with Gaussian similarity ($\sigma=1$) on both fully-connected and 10-NN graphs. Plots eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\Lun$ and $\Lrw$ illustrating that the first four eigenvectors carry the cluster information.
nodes.statement_clean: Running illustrative example showing how spectral embedding separates four clusters in 1D.

nodes.name: Cockroach graph (relaxation can be arbitrarily bad)
nodes.statement: On `cockroach' ladder-like graphs, optimal $\Ratiocut$ is a vertical cut of weight 2, but unnormalized spectral clustering produces a horizontal cut of weight $k$, giving $\Ratiocut(B,\bar B)/\Ratiocut(A,\bar A) = k/2$ - a factor on the order of $n$ worse.
nodes.statement_clean: Family of graphs where spectral relaxation has approximation factor on the order of n.

nodes.name: Two moons + Gaussian (similarity-graph comparison)
nodes.statement: Sample from two `moons' (different densities) plus a Gaussian in $\R^2$. Compares $\eps$-neighborhood, $k$-NN, and mutual $k$-NN graphs to illustrate trade-offs in connecting points across density scales.
nodes.statement_clean: Toy 2D example used to compare similarity-graph constructions.

nodes.name: Eigengap heuristic (varying Gaussian widths)
nodes.statement: Three datasets of four Gaussians with increasing variance using a 10-NN graph. As clusters become more overlapping, the gap $|\lambda_5 - \lambda_4|$ shrinks, illustrating that the eigengap heuristic works well only when clusters are well separated.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical illustration of the eigengap heuristic and its failure mode.

nodes.name: Unnormalized clustering instability with $\sigma$
nodes.statement: On the 4-Gaussian toy data with fully-connected graph and Gaussian similarity, increasing $\sigma$ pushes more eigenvalues above $\min_j d_j$. Eigenvectors with eigenvalues above $\min d_j$ approximate Dirac functions and are useless for clustering.
nodes.statement_clean: Illustrates how unnormalized spectral clustering breaks when eigenvalues approach the minimum degree.

nodes.name: $\Lun$ does not depend on diagonal of $W$
nodes.statement: Self-edges (diagonal entries of $W$) do not change the unnormalized graph Laplacian, since $D$ depends only on row sums.
nodes.statement_clean: Diagonal entries of W are irrelevant for L.

nodes.name: Quality of spectral relaxation can be unbounded
nodes.statement: The difference $\Ratiocut(B_1,\ldots,B_k) - \Ratiocut(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ between the spectral solution $B$ and optimal solution $A$ can be arbitrarily large; balanced graph cuts cannot in general be approximated up to a constant factor and the approximation problem itself is NP-hard.
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral relaxation has no general approximation guarantees for RatioCut/Ncut.

nodes.name: Spectral embedding vs commute-time embedding
nodes.statement: Spectral clustering uses rows of $U$; the commute-time embedding uses rows of $(\Lambda^\dagger)^{1/2} U$. They differ by inverse-eigenvalue scaling and the commute embedding takes all columns. They can disagree drastically (e.g. when graph has $k$ disconnected components) but agree heuristically on well-connected graphs.
nodes.statement_clean: Commute-time embedding and spectral embedding are related but not identical, with potential disagreement.

nodes.name: Why $S$ or $W$ should not replace $L$
nodes.statement: Block-diagonality is necessary but not sufficient for using eigenvectors. Two key extra properties: (i) ordering of eigenvalues must match block ordering; (ii) eigenvector entries on a block must be safely bounded away from 0. $\Lun$ and $\Lrw$ satisfy these; $S$, $W$ and (partly) $\Lsym$ do not.
nodes.statement_clean: Justifies preferring graph Laplacians to similarity/adjacency matrices for spectral clustering.

nodes.name: Recommendation: use $\Lrw$
nodes.statement: All three perspectives (graph cuts, random walks, perturbation theory) favor normalized over unnormalized clustering, and within normalized variants prefer $\Lrw$ over $\Lsym$ because its eigenvectors are exact cluster indicators rather than $D^{1/2}$-scaled versions.
nodes.statement_clean: Tutorial recommendation: use Lrw for spectral clustering when degrees vary.

nodes.name: Consistency: normalized SC converges, unnormalized may not
nodes.statement: Normalized spectral clustering with $\Lsym$ or $\Lrw$ converges as $n \to \infty$ under mild assumptions. Unnormalized SC can fail to converge or converge to trivial single-point clusters; convergence requires $\lambda_i \ll \min_j d_j$ for all eigenvectors used.
nodes.statement_clean: Consistency arguments favor normalized spectral clustering.
nodes.origin_citation: von Luxburg, Bousquet & Belkin 2004; von Luxburg, Belkin & Bousquet 2008

nodes.name: Theory of similarity-graph choice for spectral clustering
nodes.statement: No theoretical results are known on how the choice of similarity graph (type and parameters $k, \eps, \sigma$) influences the spectral clustering result. Finding theoretically justified rules of thumb is identified as an important open question.
nodes.statement_clean: Open question: principled, theory-backed selection of similarity graph and its parameters.

nodes.name: Tight relation between spectral clustering and commute distance
nodes.statement: Without further assumptions there is only a loose relation between spectral clustering and the commute distance; whether tighter precise statements exist (e.g. under strict positive-definiteness of the similarity) is left open.
nodes.statement_clean: Open: precise mathematical link between spectral embedding and commute-time embedding.

nodes.name: Interaction between number of clusters and graph connectivity parameter
nodes.statement: Beyond the case where the graph breaks into $k_0$ components, nothing non-trivial is known about how the choice of cluster number $k$ and graph connectivity parameters interact.
nodes.statement_clean: Open: principled joint selection of k and connectivity parameters.

nodes.name: Part (1): expand $f' \Lun f$
nodes.statement: By definition of $d_i$: $f'\Lun f = f'Df - f'Wf = \sum_i d_i f_i^2 - \sum_{i,j} f_i f_j w_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(f_i - f_j)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Direct algebraic expansion of the quadratic form via $f'Df - f'Wf$.

nodes.name: Part (2): symmetry and PSD
nodes.statement: Symmetry of $\Lun$ follows from symmetry of $W$ and $D$. PSD is a direct consequence of Part (1), since $f'\Lun f \geq 0$ for all $f \in \R^n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetry from W,D; positive semi-definiteness from Part (1).

nodes.name: Part (3): zero eigenvalue with $\charfct$
nodes.statement: Smallest eigenvalue $0$ with eigenvector $\charfct$: obvious from $\Lun \charfct = (D-W)\charfct = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Constant vector is zero-eigenvector by direct computation.

nodes.name: Part (4): $n$ non-negative eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Direct consequence of Parts (1)-(3): symmetric PSD matrix has $n$ real non-negative eigenvalues, the smallest being $0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combine symmetry, PSD and existence of zero eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Case $k=1$: connected graph
nodes.statement: If $f$ is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $0$: $0 = f'\Lun f = \sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(f_i-f_j)^2$. Since weights are non-negative, each term must vanish, forcing $f$ constant on each connected component; for one component, $f = a\charfct$.
nodes.statement_clean: When the graph is connected, the only zero-eigenvector is the constant vector.

nodes.name: Case general $k$: block-diagonal $\Lun$
nodes.statement: Reorder vertices by component so that $\Lun$ has block-diagonal form $\Lun = \mathrm{diag}(L_1,\ldots,L_k)$ with each $L_i$ a Laplacian of a connected subgraph. Spectrum is the union of block spectra; combine with the case $k=1$ to obtain $k$ zero eigenvalues with indicator-vector eigenvectors.
nodes.statement_clean: Block-diagonal structure plus case $k=1$ gives k zero eigenvalues with indicator-vector eigenvectors.

nodes.name: Part (1): quadratic form of $\Lsym$
nodes.statement: Proved similarly to Part (1) of Proposition \ref{prop-unnorm}, replacing $f_i$ by $f_i/\sqrt{d_i}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mirror the unnormalized expansion with rescaled coordinates.

nodes.name: Part (2): $\Lsym$-$\Lrw$ eigenpair correspondence
nodes.statement: Multiply the eigenvalue equation $\Lsym w = \lambda w$ by $D^{-1/2}$ from the left and substitute $u = D^{-1/2} w$ to obtain $\Lrw u = \lambda u$.
nodes.statement_clean: Substitute u = D^{-1/2} w in the Lsym eigenvalue equation.

nodes.name: Part (3): $\Lrw$ ↔ generalized eigenproblem
nodes.statement: Multiply $\Lrw u = \lambda u$ by $D$ from the left: $\Lun u = \lambda D u$.
nodes.statement_clean: Left-multiply by D to convert Lrw eigenproblem into generalized eigenproblem.

nodes.name: Part (4): zero eigenvalue with $\charfct$ and $D^{1/2}\charfct$
nodes.statement: $\Lrw \charfct = 0$ is direct; the $\Lsym$ statement follows from Part (2) applied to $u = \charfct$.
nodes.statement_clean: Constant vector is Lrw zero-eigenvector; transfer to Lsym via Part (2).

nodes.name: Part (5): PSD and $n$ non-negative eigenvalues
nodes.statement: PSD of $\Lsym$ follows from Part (1); PSD of $\Lrw$ follows from Part (2) (same eigenvalues).
nodes.statement_clean: Derive PSD of Lsym from quadratic form, then transfer to Lrw via eigenvalue correspondence.

nodes.name: Compute joint $P(X_0 \in A, X_1 \in B)$
nodes.statement: $P(X_0 \in A, X_1 \in B) = \sum_{i \in A, j \in B} \pi_i p_{ij} = \sum_{i\in A, j\in B} \frac{d_i}{\vol(V)} \cdot \frac{w_{ij}}{d_i} = \frac{1}{\vol(V)} \sum_{i\in A, j\in B} w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum the joint distribution under stationarity, simplifying via $\pi_i p_{ij} = w_{ij}/\vol(V)$.

nodes.name: Conditional probability $P(X_1 \in B | X_0 \in A)$
nodes.statement: $P(X_1 \in B | X_0 \in A) = \frac{P(X_0 \in A, X_1 \in B)}{P(X_0 \in A)} = \frac{(1/\vol(V)) \sum_{i\in A, j\in B} w_{ij}}{\vol(A)/\vol(V)} = \frac{\sum_{i\in A, j\in B} w_{ij}}{\vol(A)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Divide joint by marginal $\vol(A)/\vol(V)$ to get the conditional.

nodes.name: Conclude via $\Ncut$ definition
nodes.statement: Apply the definition $\Ncut(A,\bar A) = \sum_{i\in A, j\in \bar A} w_{ij}/\vol(A) + \sum_{i\in \bar A, j\in A} w_{ij}/\vol(\bar A) = P(\bar A | A) + P(A | \bar A)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recognize the two conditionals as exactly the two terms of $\Ncut(A,\bar A)$.

nodes.name: Construct similarity graph
nodes.statement: Construct a similarity graph from the data using one of the methods of Section 2 ($\eps$-neighborhood, $k$-NN, mutual $k$-NN, or fully connected). Let $W$ be its weighted adjacency matrix.
nodes.statement_clean: Build similarity graph and obtain weighted adjacency matrix W.

nodes.name: Compute unnormalized Laplacian
nodes.statement: Compute $\Lun = D - W$.
nodes.statement_clean: Compute the unnormalized graph Laplacian L = D - W.

nodes.name: Compute first $k$ eigenvectors of $\Lun$
nodes.statement: Compute the first $k$ eigenvectors $u_1,\ldots,u_k$ of $\Lun$ (corresponding to the $k$ smallest eigenvalues).
nodes.statement_clean: Eigendecomposition: take the bottom-k eigenvectors of L.

nodes.name: Form embedding matrix $U$
